parts.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: Consider what happens to the magnetic flux linked with the aluminium tube as the magnet falls through it.
Hint 2: Apply Faraday's law to explain why an electromotive force and resulting eddy currents are induced in the aluminium tube.
Hint 3: Apply Lenz's law to explain how the magnetic field of the eddy currents produces an upward opposing force on the magnet.
Hint 4: Explain the energy transfers: gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy and thermal energy in the tube via eddy current heating.
Hint 5: Conclude why the magnet in the aluminium tube accelerates at less than $g$ and reaches a terminal speed, unlike in the plastic tube.
parts.proper_answer: as magnet falls, tube cuts magnetic flux; e.m.f./(eddy) currents induced in metal/aluminium (tube); (eddy) current heating of tube; with energy taken from falling magnet; or (eddy) currents produce magnetic field (M1) that opposes motion of magnet (A1) so magnet B has acceleration < g or magnet B has smaller acceleration/reaches terminal speed
